extracted.subtask_description: Guidance entries from a newsroom diversity and style handbook covering terminology, usage, pronunciation and sensitivity guidance for reporters and editors. Each entry explains preferred terms, cautions, alternatives and contextual rules for news writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eid al-Adha
rubrics_metrics.description: A Muslim holiday tied to the hajj pilgrimage; shifts dates yearly because Muslims use a lunar calendar. Commences with the sighting of the new moon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pronunciation and contextual connection: see hajj; observe it as a feast whether or not participants are on hajj.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eid al-Fitr
rubrics_metrics.description: A joyous Islamic holiday that marks the end of Ramadan, observed with communal prayers, donations and special meals; fasting is forbidden on this day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pronounced “EED-uhl-FIT-uhr.” Shifts dates yearly because Muslims use a lunar calendar; commences with the sighting of the new moon. See Ramadan.

rubrics_metrics.name: elderly
rubrics_metrics.description: Use this word carefully and sparingly; appropriate only in generic phrases that do not refer to specific individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not describe a person as 'elderly' — permissible in generalized categories like 'concern for the elderly' or 'a home for the elderly.' To show deteriorated faculties, cite a graphic example and attribute it per AP Stylebook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emancipation Proclamation
rubrics_metrics.description: Explains scope and limitations of Lincoln's 1863 proclamation — applied only in areas of the 10 Southern states that had seceded and did not end slavery nationwide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides historical context: tied slavery to preserving the union and set the stage for the 13th Amendment; did not address slavery in Union border states. See Juneteenth for celebration of the end of slavery.

rubrics_metrics.name: eñe, ñ
rubrics_metrics.description: In Spanish, ñ is an additional letter (called an eñe), not an n with an accent, pronounced 'enye.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substituting plain n changes the word; in speech it sounds like the middle sound in 'canyon.'

rubrics_metrics.name: English-only movement
rubrics_metrics.description: Effort to make English the official language of the U.S.; about half the states have adopted such laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opponents say the laws are unnecessary, divisive and even racist.

rubrics_metrics.name: epicanthic fold
rubrics_metrics.description: See eye shape; refers to a fold often (but not exclusively) described as an 'Asian' feature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-reference to 'eye shape' entry for guidance on usage and sensitivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: epilepsy/epileptic fit
rubrics_metrics.description: A chronic neurological disorder with recurrent, unprovoked seizures; manifests differently in individuals and is most commonly treated with medication but also by devices, surgery, diet and emerging therapies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to someone as having epilepsy only if relevant and formally diagnosed. Use people-first language ('has epilepsy' not 'an epileptic'). Prefer the term 'seizure' over 'fit' or 'epileptic fit.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Episcopal Church
rubrics_metrics.description: Part of the Anglican Communion; officially the Protestant Episcopal Church in the U.S. Capitalize titles before a name but lowercase otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be clear whether a bishop is Anglican or Episcopal in disputes where congregations have broken ties; use proper honorifics (Most Rev. for presiding bishop; the Rt. Rev. for other bishops; the Rev. for priests and deacons; Very Rev., Venerable, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: equality
rubrics_metrics.description: About ensuring every individual has equal opportunity and correcting historical discrimination experienced by certain groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines groups that have experienced discrimination and states that injustices should be corrected in a just society.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eskimo
rubrics_metrics.description: Term for indigenous peoples of Arctic regions; controversial and should be used with caution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many consider it derogatory; Canada/Greenland prefer 'Inuit' or local terms. In Alaska many still accept 'Eskimo.' Best practice: ask individuals or community leaders what they prefer. Note federal laws replaced 'Eskimo' with 'Alaska Native' in 2016 (HR 4238).

rubrics_metrics.name: ethnic
rubrics_metrics.description: Frequently used to describe non-Western/Non-North American things; connotes otherness and can be marginalizing or offensive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid; use the specific country or culture (e.g., 'Thai food') or terms like international music, global food, world cuisine. Do not use 'ethnic' to describe a person. Exception: academic field 'ethnic studies.' Includes citations for further reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: ethnic group
rubrics_metrics.description: Caution; vague — a group self-identifying by geographical, linguistic, cultural, religious and other ties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes historical use equating 'ethnic group' with 'race' in the 19th/20th centuries (e.g., 'the Hungarian race').

rubrics_metrics.name: ethnicity, mention of
rubrics_metrics.description: A person's ethnicity should not be mentioned unless relevant; this applies to ethnicity, sexual orientation and religion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derogatory terms or slurs may only be used if directly relevant and approved by senior editor. Avoid stereotypes. Lists contexts where race/ethnicity may be relevant (crime descriptions — include detailed, attributed descriptions; biographical/announcement stories — reserve race/ethnicity for significant 'firsts' or historic events). See race.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evangelical Lutheran Church in America
rubrics_metrics.description: Largest Lutheran denomination in the U.S.; ELCA is acceptable on second reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not confuse with the Lutheran Church-Missouri Synod, which is smaller and more conservative. See Lutheran.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Order 9066
rubrics_metrics.description: 1942 war measure leading to internment of about 117,000 people of Japanese heritage; two-thirds were U.S. citizens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes cabinet division, exemptions for other heritage groups, Supreme Court affirmations, and Congress's 1983 declaration calling it 'a grave injustice.' Cross-references Angel Island and internment, Japanese.

rubrics_metrics.name: exotic
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid; when describing women of Asian and Pacific Islander heritage it implies deviation from a white norm and can be racist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes reference to essay critiquing use of 'exotic.'

rubrics_metrics.name: eye shape, reference to
rubrics_metrics.description: Misnomer — all human eyeballs have the same shape; the distinctive 'Asian' feature is the epicanthic fold but not all Asians have it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not call eyes 'slanted' or 'slitty' (derogatory). Explain relevance of discussing the fold to avoid racial stereotyping (e.g., legitimate contexts: plastic surgery discussion).

rubrics_metrics.name: fag, faggot
rubrics_metrics.description: A pejorative term for a gay male and extremely offensive when used as an epithet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only in a quotation if there is a compelling reason.

rubrics_metrics.name: family
rubrics_metrics.description: Proper term for identifying a family led by LGBT parents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify parents' sexual orientation only when germane. Do not use 'gay families.' Mention genetic relationships or conception techniques only when germane. See parent.

rubrics_metrics.name: fat
rubrics_metrics.description: See obese, obesity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-reference to the obesity guidance rather than using 'fat.'

rubrics_metrics.name: fatwa
rubrics_metrics.description: A legal pronouncement issued by an Islamic scholar; no central authority and pertains only to Muslims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expert must have rigorously studied the Quran and be aware of all elements of the case. Fatwas are not binding in secular settings; they usually give religious guidance. Violent or death fatwas are rare.

rubrics_metrics.name: felon, offender
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid these terms when referring to someone convicted of a crime because they label people by the crime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use people-first language and specific phrasing: 'was convicted of felony robbery,' 'is registered as a sex offender in [state],' 'was on trial for criminal loitering,' 'was placed on probation.' The Marshall Project recommends avoiding dehumanizing labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: female/feminine pronouns, male/masculine pronouns
rubrics_metrics.description: Not all people who use she/her are women, and not all who use he/him are men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the term 'pronouns' or 'she/her pronouns' or 'he/him pronouns' to be precise; avoid assuming pronouns equal gender.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filipino/Pilipino
rubrics_metrics.description: Refers to an inhabitant of the Philippines; Filipino American refers to those sharing its heritage and culture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some prefer 'Pilipino' because Tagalog lacks an 'F' sound. See Tagalog. Historical note on Philippines named after King Philip II.

rubrics_metrics.name: First Nations
rubrics_metrics.description: Term for Aboriginal peoples of Canada who are neither Métis nor Inuit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replaced 'Indian' in common usage since the 1970s/80s; not widely used in the U.S. (Updated February 2021).

rubrics_metrics.name: First World
rubrics_metrics.description: Outdated term referring to developed, capitalist countries used during the Cold War model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend using 'developed world' and 'developing world' instead; see Third World.

rubrics_metrics.name: fixer
rubrics_metrics.description: In journalism, a local person who helps reporters in foreign countries with arranging interviews, translating, interpreting and local expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Term can be seen as demeaning; alternatives include 'local reporting partner,' 'local correspondent,' or 'local journalist' (Updated March 2021).

rubrics_metrics.name: flip
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid; pejorative term for Filipino.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use.

rubrics_metrics.name: fortune cookie
rubrics_metrics.description: Origin almost certainly Japanese despite common association with China.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: China and Japan do not have a tradition of dessert following a meal; historical references indicate Japanese origins.

rubrics_metrics.name: FTM / MTF / FTN / MTN / FT* / MT*
rubrics_metrics.description: Acronyms describing transgender or transsexual individuals (from assigned birth sex to affirmed gender).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First letter is assigned birth sex, second letter T is 'to' (transition), third letter is destination gender. The * indicates inclusivity for variations of trans people.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fu Manchu
rubrics_metrics.description: Stereotyped literary villain created in 1913; caution advised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes historical racist portrayals and the 'yellow peril' stereotype and later similar villains. Avoid stereotypical invocations.

rubrics_metrics.name: fundamentalism, fundamentalist
rubrics_metrics.description: Originally a U.S. Christian movement emphasizing biblical inerrancy; term has broadened and can be pejorative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists often (erroneously) label conservative Christians as fundamentalists; best to avoid unless a group applies the term to itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: gay
rubrics_metrics.description: Refers to men attracted to other men; preferred over 'homosexual' which is clinical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid using as a singular noun; for women use 'lesbian' unless subject prefers otherwise. Use 'gays and lesbians' to include both; in headlines 'gay' may be acceptable to describe both.

rubrics_metrics.name: geezer
rubrics_metrics.description: Ageist terminology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid.

rubrics_metrics.name: gender assigned at birth (GAAB), MAAB, FAAB
rubrics_metrics.description: The gender a person is assigned at birth, referenced because it may not be the person's true gender.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See transgender; explains MAAB/FAAB acronyms.

rubrics_metrics.name: gender binary
rubrics_metrics.description: The assumption that gender is only male and female and that they are distinct and disconnected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many view this as a false dichotomy given intersex, transgender and agender identities. See related entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: gender dysphoria
rubrics_metrics.description: DSM-V term replacing 'Gender Identity Disorder' with changed diagnostic criteria; necessity of diagnosis remains controversial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Psychiatric/medical authorities recommend individualized treatment; some advocates see DSM inclusion as necessary for insurance coverage. Ask people with gender dysphoria which pronouns they prefer.

rubrics_metrics.name: gender expansive
rubrics_metrics.description: Used for people who challenge cultural expectations around gender roles, identities, expressions or norms; includes a range of identities and expressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some may identify as man/woman, some neither, some on a spectrum. Some use gender-neutral pronouns. See agender, genderqueer, transgender. (Updated February 2021)

rubrics_metrics.name: gender expression
rubrics_metrics.description: External manifestations of gender expressed through name, pronouns, clothing, haircut, behavior, voice or body characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Society labels cues as masculine/feminine though definitions vary; transgender people seek alignment of expression with identity. See gender-expansive, transgender.

rubrics_metrics.name: gender fluidity
rubrics_metrics.description: Conveys a flexible range of gender expression that may change over time or day-to-day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Children may feel like a girl some days and a boy other days, or neither. Ask people which pronouns they prefer. See gender-expansive.

rubrics_metrics.name: gender identity
rubrics_metrics.description: One's internal, deeply held sense of gender; for transgender people this may not match sex assigned at birth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most people identify as man or woman, but some do not fit those categories; gender identity is internal and not visible. See gender expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gender Identity Disorder
rubrics_metrics.description: Outdated term; avoid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See gender dysphoria.

rubrics_metrics.name: gender nonconforming
rubrics_metrics.description: Describes people whose gender expression differs from conventional expectations; not synonymous with transgender.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only if someone self-identifies as such; not all transgender people are gender non-conforming. Ask which pronouns they prefer.

rubrics_metrics.name: gender normative
rubrics_metrics.description: Refers to people whose sex assignment at birth corresponds to gender identity and expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See cisgender, cis.

rubrics_metrics.name: gender role
rubrics_metrics.description: Set of roles, activities and expectations assigned to females and males by society; typically masculine and feminine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: People who step outside roles may be referred to as transgender; other cultures may recognize more than two gender roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: gender spectrum
rubrics_metrics.description: Model that breaks the binary and accounts for infinite variations of gender.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when discussing non-binary conceptions of gender.

rubrics_metrics.name: gender transition
rubrics_metrics.description: Process by which transgender people change physical/sexual characteristics associated with sex assigned at birth; may include social, legal and medical steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May include name/legal document changes, hormone therapy, sometimes surgery. Not synonymous with 'sexual reassignment.' Avoid outdated 'sex change.'

rubrics_metrics.name: gender variant
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid unless in academic writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer other, more current terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: gender-affirming care/transition-related medical care
rubrics_metrics.description: Broad term for health care transgender people may pursue, including counseling, hormone therapy and surgeries; not all pursue all treatments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use general language unless specifics are necessary; use official names of procedures when appropriate. Avoid 'mastectomy' for transmasculine chest surgery—use 'chest reconstruction surgery' or 'chest masculinization surgery.' See Trans Journalists Association guidance. (Updated March 2021)

rubrics_metrics.name: gender-bender, gender-bending
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual who intentionally does not conform to binary gender roles or expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only if self-referential or in quotation with a compelling reason; as an adjective, use 'gender-bending.'

rubrics_metrics.name: gender-neutral pronouns
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternatives to traditional pronouns used by people whose gender identity is not male or female.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If someone doesn't identify as male or female, ask which pronouns they use. Includes updated alternatives (Updated 3/1/2021).

rubrics_metrics.name: genderqueer
rubrics_metrics.description: Term for people whose gender identity/expression falls outside 'man' or 'woman'; not synonymous with transgender.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only if self-identified. People may not feel comfortable with standard pronouns; ask which pronouns to use. See agender, transgender, gender non-conforming.

rubrics_metrics.name: genocide
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliberate killing of a large group, especially of a particular ethnic, religious, linguistic, racial or cultural group; a specific legal term defined by international convention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains origins of the term (Lemkin) and the 1948 UN Convention definition listing acts (killing, causing serious harm, inflicting destructive conditions, preventing births, forcible transfer of children). Use carefully given legal specificity.

rubrics_metrics.name: gentile
rubrics_metrics.description: In Judaism, anyone who is not a Jew; usually a reference to Christians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some Mormons use the term to describe non-Mormons.

rubrics_metrics.name: gerontology/geriatrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Gerontology studies social, psychological and biological aspects of aging; geriatrics is the medical branch studying diseases and health of older people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish the fields when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: ghetto
rubrics_metrics.description: Term used as a synonym for city sections inhabited by poor people or minorities; has negative connotations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid; prefer the neighborhood name, or neutral terms like section, district or quarter.

rubrics_metrics.name: God
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize in reference to all monotheistic religions and terms like God the Father; lowercase personal pronouns (him, he).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be sensitive to context and avoid gender-defining pronouns when appropriate. Use 'G-d' in quotes of written material for Orthodox Jews who avoid spelling the name, but otherwise use 'God.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Good Friday
rubrics_metrics.description: Christian observance commemorating the crucifixion of Jesus, falling before Easter Sunday.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of Holy Week; use in appropriate religious context.

rubrics_metrics.name: good name
rubrics_metrics.description: Phrase confusion in India: 'What is your good name?' simply asks for a person's name (literal translation of Hindi).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of differences in literal translations and intended meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gospel, gospel
rubrics_metrics.description: Derives from Old English 'Godspell' meaning 'good news'; refers to the four New Testament books (Matthew, Mark, Luke, John).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capitalize when referring to the first four books; lowercase in other references.

rubrics_metrics.name: grandfather in, grandfather clause
rubrics_metrics.description: Exempting people from a change because of preexisting conditions (e.g., older buildings exempted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Term originated in the American South to enfranchise poor white people and disenfranchise Black people; use with caution. 'Legacy' can be an alternative phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Great Migration, the
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-Reconstruction U.S. movement (c.1916–1970) of some 6 million African Americans from South to North seeking safety and opportunity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes context about fleeing lynchings and facing new forms of segregation in housing, education and employment.

rubrics_metrics.name: green card
rubrics_metrics.description: United States Permanent Resident Card (actually pink) allowing permanent residence and work; holder is not a U.S. citizen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asking Latinos born in U.S. or Puerto Ricans whether they have a green card can be insulting; see immigrant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gullah
rubrics_metrics.description: Creole blend of Elizabethan English and African languages developed in slave communities on the coastal South and Sea Islands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical context about isolation and persistence of the Gullah speech; see Creole.

rubrics_metrics.name: gurdwara
rubrics_metrics.description: A Sikh place of worship that houses the Guru Granth Sahib (Sikh scripture).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use term when describing Sikh places of worship; factual description.

rubrics_metrics.name: guru
rubrics_metrics.description: Teacher in Hinduism, Sikhism and Buddhism; in popular English means any knowledgeable guide or mentor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriately depending on religious or colloquial context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gypsy
rubrics_metrics.description: Word used to indicate Roma people; has negative connotations and many Roma consider it a racial slur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer 'Roma people' unless people self-identify as 'Gypsies' (capitalize then). Avoid casual/pejorative uses (e.g., 'they lived like gypsies') and the pejorative 'gyp' (likely derived from Gypsy). (Updated February 2021)

rubrics_metrics.name: hadith
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports about sayings/actions/traditions of Muhammad and his companions; pronounced 'ha-DEETH.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as singular and plural; viewed by Muslims as explanations of the Quran and second only to it in guidance. Two most reliable collections are by Bukhari and Muslim.

rubrics_metrics.name: hair, African American or Black
rubrics_metrics.description: When describing a person's hair, ask what style it is; Black hair comes in a variety of styles and textures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides list of styles (afro, bald/shaved distinction, braids/plaits, cornrows/French braids, dreadlocks/locs, extensions, Jheri curl, twists, weave). Suggests using questions about hair to open larger conversations; references a video 'Five Questions About Black Hair.'

rubrics_metrics.name: hajj
rubrics_metrics.description: Pronounced 'hahj.' Islam pilgrimage to Mecca; fifth pillar of Islam; every capable Muslim expected to make it once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Takes place during 12th month with specific five-day rites; dates move yearly with lunar calendar. 'hajj' typically not capitalized. A 'hajji' is a person who undertook the pilgrimage. See Eid al-Adha.

rubrics_metrics.name: halakhah
rubrics_metrics.description: Pronounced 'ha-la-KHAH.' Jewish law governing aspects of life, defined by scripture and teachings and interpreted by rabbis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains belief in law given at Sinai and ongoing rabbinic interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: halal
rubrics_metrics.description: In Arabic, means lawful and permitted in Islam; refers to permissible foods, objects and activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Halal slaughter requires invoking God's name and draining blood; pork and intoxicants are not halal. Forbidden items are 'haram.'

rubrics_metrics.name: hamesh hand
rubrics_metrics.description: Hamesh is the Hebrew word for hamsa in Arabic, meaning five or 'five fingers of the hand.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in Jewish/Israeli culture; often adorned with Star of David or Hebrew letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: hamsa
rubrics_metrics.description: Palm-shaped symbol for good luck or protection predating Islam, seen in many cultures; sometimes called 'hand of Fatima' by some Muslims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-religious symbol adopted across traditions and cultures.
